solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rubbish with unpleasant smell attracting insect

parts.note: a hum is informal British slang for a bad smell
a bug is any small insect

explanation.surface: Some foul-smelling refuse is drawing flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' just joins the smell to the insect, which follows it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug is nonsense or deceptive talk, so it means rubbish in the sense of drivel.

clue.text: Figure pathogen spread

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A diagram shows how a germ is spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Rough-and-ready model dress

parts.note: a make is a model or brand of product
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: A fashion model's outfit looks hastily thrown together.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift describes something improvised, rough and temporary.

clue.text: In court Bellow causes confusion

parts.note: to be up before a magistrate is to be in court
to roar is to bellow

explanation.surface: A loud shout in the courtroom causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bellow' is capitalised as if it were the novelist Saul Bellow, but it is just a loud shout.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud disturbance, noisy confusion.

clue.text: Gloomy, unused actors

parts.note: food left over is unused, so over can mean surplus or unused
the cast of a play is its body of actors

explanation.surface: Performers left out of a production are feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky covered in cloud is dull and dark, hence gloomy weather.

clue.text: Goddess seen in play

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
observed means seen

explanation.surface: A deity appears in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus Observed is a 1950 verse drama by Christopher Fry, so it is a play.

clue.text: See the light in effect

definitions.meaning: to see the light is to come to understand, to grasp at last
to put a plan in effect is to make it real or achieve it

explanation.definitionFit: To realise means both to understand something suddenly and to bring a plan into actual being.

clue.text: Belonging to a famous group from Nepal is Tenzing

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A Himalayan climber from Nepal is part of an elite.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft split 'group' from the definition; the definition is 'Belonging to a famous group' and 'from' alone signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A-list describes the top celebrities, the most famous group of people.

clue.text: Testing hearing

definitions.meaning: something testing is hard to bear, wearing on the patience
a judge hearing a case is putting someone on trial

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both exasperating and conducting a court trial, as in a judge examining a case.

clue.text: US writer holding king and queen in card game

indicators.note: the writer's name holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author of tales of mystery
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An American author is clutching two royal cards during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known betting game played with hands of five cards.

clue.text: Lying soldiers beginning to deceive a large town

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for soldiers or troops

indicators.note: beginning to says only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Troops start to mislead an entire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is the habit of telling untruths, so it is the noun for lying.

clue.text: One with global experience?

parts.note: literally someone who knows the whole globe; idiomatically a sophisticated, worldly person

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a cultured, experienced person who knows how the world works.

clue.text: Avoid a black spot

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a dark mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from or decline something, as a voter may.

clue.text: Dairy product in list boy brought round

indicators.note: the leaning word sits in the boy, which is the container
the boy is brought round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a son is a boy
to list is to lean over, as a ship does, which is to tilt

explanation.surface: A dairy item appears on a shopping list a lad has carried home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is not a written list but a ship's lean to one side; the boy is brought round that lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous English blue cheese, which is a dairy product.

clue.text: Sculptor has no right to show a Norse god

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: An artist who lacks permission depicts a Scandinavian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor.

clue.text: Ball cancelled prior to holiday

indicators.note: prior to places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: an event that is called off is cancelled
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A dance is scrapped just before the vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' looks like a dance, but it is a cricket delivery: an off-break is a ball that spins in from the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an off-break is a type of spun delivery, i.e. a kind of ball bowled.

clue.text: Hold on to part of record to remain informed

parts.note: to keep something is to retain it rather than let it go
a track is one song on an album or record

explanation.surface: Hang on to a song from the album so as to stay up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep track is to stay aware of developments, i.e. to stay informed.

clue.text: Game bird shot in a Borsetshire village

indicators.note: shot suggests the letters are blasted apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pheasant is shot in a rural English village.
explanation.walkthrough: Borsetshire is the fictional county of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap about English farming life.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambridge is the fictional village in Borsetshire where The Archers is set.

clue.text: Be careful of a heartless knave employed by the editor

indicators.note: employed by is read as taken into, so the first pieces go inside the later ones

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes the inner letters, keeping only the outside ones

explanation.surface: Watch out for a callous rogue hired by the newspaper chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the three middle letters of 'knave'; 'employed by' puts the result, after A, into the editor phrase just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heed of something is to pay attention to it, being careful about it.

clue.text: Most agreeable sort set free

parts.note: a kind is a sort or type

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: The nicest kind of person releases a captive.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindest is the superlative of kind, meaning most pleasant and agreeable.

clue.text: Appear in bishop's office before mass

indicators.note: before puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: a see is the seat or jurisdiction of a bishop
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Show up at the bishop's headquarters ahead of the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to appear to be something, as in giving an impression.

clue.text: Badly handle creeping plant round end of barn

indicators.note: round means the plant word goes around the next piece

parts.note: bugle is a low creeping plant with blue flowers

indicators.note: end of takes only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Clumsily dealing with a creeper growing around a farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle is to botch or mishandle a task.

clue.text: When this is not shown old lady makes a complaint

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: not shown means the following word is removed from the previous one

parts.note: taken as written
one's old lady can be one's mother, ma

explanation.surface: An elderly woman grumbles when something is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this is not shown' leaves TH once IS is removed; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is an illness, and complaint can mean an ailment.

clue.text: So far ahead, small number in tug

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead

indicators.note: in puts the small number inside the word for tug

parts.note: to tow is to tug or pull
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Leading the way, a little figure on a tugboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to now is an idiom for until the present time, i.e. so far.

clue.text: Left in current accent

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for current

parts.note: a tide is a current of water

explanation.surface: Departed in a modern style of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy accent mark placed over a letter, as in Spanish.

clue.text: Peak on cap worn by Italian tourist

indicators.note: worn by means the cap part wraps around the other piece, as clothing wraps its wearer

parts.note: a visor is the peak projecting from the front of a cap

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker from Italy wears a peaked cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone paying a visit to a place, a sightseer.

clue.text: Information supplied by staff about early garden plant

indicators.note: about means the information word is placed around the next piece

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
old can mean early, as in the old days
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Advice given by gardening staff on an early-flowering plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied by' just joins the pieces; 'early' as old is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a plant with tall spikes of yellow flowers grown in gardens.

clue.text: Difficult getting round in store

indicators.note: getting is read as taking in, so the round letter goes inside

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: It is tough to get around the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile, which is a store of things kept away.

clue.text: Endless thought given to incident in the latter part of the day

definitions.text: the latter part of the day

parts.note: an event is an incident

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped from the word for thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: Unending reflection on something that happened late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' joins EVENT and IDE (IDEA with its last letter removed by 'Endless').
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the later part of the day.

clue.text: Take hold of two animals brought round

indicators.note: brought round means the animal pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cat is a common animal

explanation.surface: Get a grip on a couple of creatures being led back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' turns both animals backwards together, so the second animal ends up first.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle is to grab or seize, as in tackling an opponent.
